story_type: untethered jetpack astronaut fails to grab a tumbling satellite, shuttle crew film 1984
hook: No tether, a jetpack, and a satellite that would not hold still.
narration: No tether. Just a jetpack, and a satellite that would not hold still.
April 1984. The shuttle Challenger chased down the broken Solar Max satellite, two hundred fifty miles up.
Pinky Nelson flew out of the bay on a jetpack called the MMU, with a docking tool on the front.
The MMU fires small jets of nitrogen gas, so an astronaut can fly free with nothing tying him to the ship.
He went in to dock. The tool hit a pin on the satellite and bounced right off.
He tried three times. Each time he bounced away as fast as he went in.
[short pause] So he grabbed a solar panel by hand. The satellite started to tumble even more.
The shuttle's robot arm kept missing it. Once it came within inches.
The ground said they might be able to steady it, so the crew backed off to try another day.
On the next try it was turning slowly, and the arm went in for it.
outcome: The arm caught Solar Max, and the crew locked it in the bay and repaired it in space.
title: Bounced off a tumbling satellite
description:
In April 1984, on shuttle flight STS-41C, astronaut Pinky Nelson flew an untethered jetpack to the tumbling Solar Max satellite, but his docking tool bounced off. Challenger's arm caught the satellite on a later try and the crew repaired it in orbit. From the crew's own post flight film.

Footage: NASA video (Space Shuttle Flight 11, STS-41C Post Flight Presentation), via Wikimedia Commons: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Space_Shuttle_Flight_11_(STS-41C)_Post_Flight_Presentation.webm
